title: unit-gap-certificates: machine-checkable artefacts for a refutation of Theorem 2 of arXiv:2603.08033

creators.name: Busnello, Luiz Antonio
creators.affiliation: Curious Tech Entrepreneur, São Paulo, Brazil

description:
DRAT proof certificates, exhaustive NPN-class gap censuses, exact-synthesis encoders, and a Lean 4 formalization supporting a refutation of Theorem 2 of Krinkin, The Unit Gap: How Sharing Works in Boolean Circuits (arXiv:2603.08033).

What this is not: progress on P vs NP. It is a correction to one published claim about the gap between DAG-optimal and formula-optimal And-Inverter Graph size, plus the data behind it.

The counterexample is parity on three inputs, where the DAG optimum is 6 gates and the formula optimum is 9, so the gap is 3 rather than the claimed maximum of 1. Both endpoints are classical: the AIG basis with free inversions is exactly U2 (the full binary basis minus XOR and XNOR), so Schnorr (1976) gives 3n-3 for the circuit side — an equality restated in the openly accessible Morizumi, arXiv:1504.06731, since the 1976 original is not — and Lee (STACS 2007) gives the exact De Morgan formula size for the formula side. That identification is elementary, but it is a step, and it is supplied by the accompanying note rather than by Schnorr or Lee. The artefacts here replicate the two values mechanically — the DRAT certificates on the circuit side, the Lean development on the formula side — rather than carry the argument.

An exhaustive census over the 222 NPN classes of n = 4 finds 72 classes (32.4%) with gap at least 2, the maximum being 6 — which is exactly what Schnorr and Lee predict for parity-4, an external check on the pipeline.

The DRAT proofs are self-contained: re-checking them requires only drat-trim, not the encoder or the solver. See README.md for the claim-to-file table and the re-check command.
